newsitem.title: USA: HFS in talks to acquire 2nd car rental firm.
newsitem.headline: HFS in talks to acquire 2nd car rental firm.

text.p: HFS Inc Tuesday said it is in talks to acquire a second car rental firm just as the company is about to complete the $800 million acquisition of Avis Inc.
"We're quite far along," in the acquisition of the unidentified company HFS Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Henry Silverman told investors at the Montgomery Securities Conference here.
Silverman said he hoped to complete the acquisition of Avis by October 11.

In August HFS announced it reached a definitive agreement with General Motors Corp to acquire its interest in Avis. The hotel and real estate franchiser, whichs owns Century 21 Real Estate Corp, Coldwell Banker Corp. and several hotel franchises, already reached agreements with the Avis Employee Stock Ownership Trust and Avis Inc. Avis, the nation's second largest rental car agency, is 71 percent-owned by employees.

At the conference, Silverman said HFS plans to sell 75 percent of Avis in 1997 to investors as a newly-public company. HFS will keep the Avis name and the new company will be the biggest Avis franchiser.

Silverman said the Avis acqusition could add as much as $0.30 a share to HFS earnings in 1997. According to analysts, the company is expected to earn around $2 a share in 1997. Silverman said the estimates do not include the second car rental acqusition, which he said the company hopes to announce this quarter.

HFS has increased its revenue in the past five years by aggressively acquiring two or three rival businesses in a particular industry. The acquisition of a second car rental company would be in step with that strategy, said Mike Mueller, an analyst at Montgomery Securities.
The acquisiton of the second car rental company also would help HFS reduce the cost of operating its Avis fleet," Silverman said.

Industry analysts said Chrysler Corp would be the most likely candidate to sell one of its car rental companies because it has previously discussed such a move as part of its efforts to focus on its core businesses.
Chrysler currently operates Dollar Rent-A-Car and Thrfity Rent-A-Car.
Chrysler declined to comment on whether it is in talks with HFS.
